extracted.intended_audience: trade mark applicants, patent/trade mark practitioners, and Patent Office staff (United Kingdom, commentary on Trade Marks Act 1883)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal standards for applying for and obtaining trade mark registration in the United Kingdom under the Trade Marks Act 1883, covering definitions, required forms/representations, advertisement, opposition, appeals, series/colour rules, and assignment with goodwill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Design'
rubrics_metrics.description: "Design" means any design applicable to any article of manufacture, or to any substance artificial or natural, or partly artificial and partly natural, whether the design is applicable for the pattern, or for the shape or configuration, or for the ornament thereof, or for any two or more of such purposes, and by whatever means it is applicable ... not being a design for a sculpture, or other thing within the protection of the Sculpture Copyright Act of 1814.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is broad: applicability may be for pattern, shape/configuration, ornament, or combinations; applicability by any manual, mechanical or chemical means (printing, painting, embroidering, weaving, modelling, casting, embossing, engraving, staining, etc.). Sculptures/models are excluded under the Sculpture Copyright Act 1814.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Copyright' in designs
rubrics_metrics.description: "Copyright" means the exclusive right to apply a design to any article of manufacture or to any such substance as aforesaid in the class or classes in which the design is registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exclusive right is limited to the class or classes for which the design is registered; it does not authorize application to articles outside the registered class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who is 'Proprietor' of a design
rubrics_metrics.description: The author of any new and original design shall be considered the proprietor thereof, unless he executed the work on behalf of another for a good or valuable consideration; persons acquiring for value, acquiring limited rights, or persons on whom property devolves are proprietors to the extent of their acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four categories enumerated: (1) author, (2) purchaser for value, (3) purchaser of limited rights for value, (4) successor on whom the property devolves. Definition taken from prior statute; applies to extent of acquisition only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller's power to register trade marks and required form
rubrics_metrics.description: The comptroller may, on application by or on behalf of any person claiming to be proprietor, register the trade mark; the application must be made in the form set forth in the First Schedule (Form F) or other prescribed form and left at or sent to the Patent Office in the prescribed manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must follow prescribed Trade Mark Forms and Rules. Stamped forms (5d) are used; separate application required per class. Applications may be signed by applicant or authorised agent (agent must sign as 'agent'); firm members or company officers may sign in specified ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and nature of representations to accompany application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be accompanied by the prescribed number of representations of the trade mark and must state the particular goods or classes of goods in connexion with which registration is desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribed number varies by classes (instructions indicate three additional representations for most classes, two for some cotton-related classes, etc.). Where representation exceeds form space, it must be backed with linen, folded and affixed. If the mark contains non‑Roman characters, a translation must be given on the form and each representation. For metal goods (other than certain categories) the metal(s) must be stated. For classes 23–25 (cotton goods) applicant must state the name by which mark will be referred in invoices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction of claim when goods indicated on mark face
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is an indication on the face of the mark of the goods to which the mark is applied, the claim for registration must be restricted to those goods only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the mark itself specifies goods, applicant cannot claim broader classes; Trade Mark Instructions require restriction in such cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series of marks — when and how they may be registered
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person claims several trade marks which resemble one another in material particulars but differ in respect of the statement of the goods, numbers, price, quality, or names of places, such marks may be registered as a series in one registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must contain representation of each mark in the series and required number of additional representations. A series is assignable/transmissible only as a whole, but for other purposes each mark is treated as separately registered. Fees differ for series (one fee for first mark, smaller fee for additional marks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisement of application and provision of wood blocks/electrotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: The application will be advertised in the Trade Marks Journal; on demand the comptroller may require the applicant to furnish a wood block or electrotype for each mark in each class (with exceptions for certain cotton classes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blocks/electrotypes must correspond exactly with the representation, be marked with the number given by the comptroller, must not exceed specified dimensions (8.5 by 10 inches), and extra charges apply if depth >2 inches. Blocks/electrotypes will not be returned. In a series, a block/electrotype is needed for each mark of each class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for registration after advertisement and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: A mark will not be registered until two months after its advertisement and then, if there is no opposition, the comptroller may enter it upon the register on receipt of the prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees: prescribed amounts per mark per class (text example: 1 pound for each mark for each class; for series specified amounts for first and additional marks). Fees paid by sending Form I stamped with the proper amount. Notice of registration will be sent to applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Death of applicant before registration
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant dies before registration is completed the comptroller may, if satisfied of the applicant's death, enter on the register as proprietor the person owning the goodwill of the business, if such ownership is proved to the satisfaction of the comptroller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comptroller requires satisfactory proof that the person claiming is the owner of the business goodwill; Trade Marks Rules cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure on refusal to register and right to be heard
rubrics_metrics.description: The comptroller may refuse to register a trade mark, but before so doing must give the applicant ten days' notice of the time when he may be heard personally or by agent; the applicant must give notice within five days if he desires to be heard; the applicant will be heard and the decision notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If final decision adverse, applicant may appeal within one month to the Board of Trade (Form H) with a statement of grounds and case. The Board may hear or refer appeal to Court. Rules give particulars on notices and forms and hearing directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment for failure to complete within 12 months due to applicant default
rubrics_metrics.description: Where registration has not been completed within twelve months from date of application by reason of default on part of applicant, the application shall be deemed to be abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section applies only where default is on applicant's part; does not apply where delay is due to other causes (e.g., appeal to Board of Trade).

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential particulars making up a trade mark
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of the Act a trade mark must consist of or contain at least one of: (a) a name of an individual or firm printed, impressed, or woven in some particular and distinctive manner; (b) a written signature or copy of a written signature of the individual or firm applying for registration; (c) a distinctive device, mark, brand, heading, label, ticket, or fancy word or words not in common use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additions of letters, words or figures are permitted. Class (b) requires the signature to be that of the applicant. Class (c) requires distinctiveness; the Rules and Instructions list devices not regarded as distinctive. Fancy words must not be in common use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of 'old' marks (used before 13 August 1875)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special and distinctive word(s), letter, figure or combinations used as a trade mark before 13 August 1875 may be registered as an old trade mark under subsection (3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two conditions: (1) used as a trade mark prior to 13 August 1875; (2) must be 'a special and distinctive' mark. 'Old' refers to use on the goods. Under the 'Three Mark Rule,' no more than three persons can register the same old mark where public use by more than three makes it common to the trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctiveness requirements and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: A mark (device, word, letter, figure) must be 'distinctive' to be registrable; many common devices or words will be refused unless distinctive character is shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: specially invented words (e.g., 'Lacto Peptine', 'Cocoatina') are favorable; foreign words may be registrable (with translation if non‑Roman characters); names of places can be good marks where they denote manufacturer (e.g., 'Anatolia', 'Glenfield'); initials may be registered when combined with distinctive device; single letters generally not registrable under 1875 Act but may be under subsection (3). A device ordinarily means representation of an object (bell, lion) — list of non‑distinctive devices published by Registry (instructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited or specially restricted matter in representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain representations should not appear in the representation forms and certain depicted elements will not be registered unless used before 13 August 1875.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples prohibited in representations: the Royal arms or similar, words like 'Registered', 'Registered Design', 'Copyright', 'Entered at Stationers' Hall', 'To counterfeit this is Forgery', 'Patent', 'Patented'. Elements not registerable (unless pre‑1875 use): portraits of Her Majesty or Royal Family, Royal Crown, national arms or flags, prize/exhibition medals. Ornamental or coloured groundworks (tartans/checks) cannot be claimed as part of a mark unless included by border or lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration must be for particular goods or classes; class system
rubrics_metrics.description: A trade mark must be registered for particular goods or classes of goods; registration is organized into fifty classes (per Trade Marks Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If doubt arises about which class a description of goods belongs to, the comptroller determines the class. A mark that indicates the goods must be restricted to those goods. Old marks and new marks may be registered for part of a class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees, representations and form availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are made on stamped forms; stamped forms obtainable at Patent Office and chief post offices; fees depend on class and whether series; number of representations prescribed by class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: three representations for classes 1–22 and 36–50, two for classes 23–35 in some instructions; series fees: fee on application and a specific registration fee breakdown. Payment by sending Form I with proper stamp amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration in colour and treatment of coloured groundworks
rubrics_metrics.description: A trade mark may be registered in any colour and such registration confers exclusive right to use the same in that or any other colour (subject to Act provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, ornamental or coloured groundworks (tartans, checks) cannot be claimed as part of the mark unless the groundwork is included within the mark by some border or lines (per Trade Marks Instructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to registration — notice, counter-statement, and security for costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may within two months of the first advertisement give notice in duplicate at the Patent Office of opposition to registration; applicant may send a counter‑statement within two months after receipt of such notice or be deemed to have abandoned the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition notice requires a 1 shilling stamp and must state grounds. If opponent gives notice, the comptroller requires him to give security for costs (in manner/amount the comptroller may require) within 14 days or opposition is deemed withdrawn. If security is given, the case stands for determination of the Court; requisite forms (Form J for opposition, Form X for counter-statement) and procedural rules govern steps. Applicant may object to solvency of security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when case stands for Court and applicant's rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Where opposition causes the case to stand for the Court, the applicant within one month may issue a summons in the High Court for an order to register notwithstanding the opposition and must give notice to the comptroller (copy of summons endorsed for service). Comptroller may require other proceedings; failure to take proceedings within time leads to abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant must leave an office copy of any successful order at the Patent Office for register rectification. Trade Marks Rules set time limits and forms for these steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and transmission only in connection with goodwill
rubrics_metrics.description: A trade mark, when registered, shall be assignable and transmissible only in connexion with the goodwill of the business concerned in the particular trademark, and shall be determinable with that goodwill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At common law a trade mark can only be assigned/transmitted with the business goodwill; sale of goodwill transfers trade marks. The sale need not be in writing or by deed. The registration form for assignee asks for particulars of assignment (e.g., deed date) but a deed may not strictly be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three‑Mark Rule for old marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the 'Three Mark Rule,' no more than three persons can register the same old mark; if a mark is publicly used by more than three persons it is to be deemed common to the trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits the number of registrations of identical 'old' marks (marks in use before 13 Aug 1875) to prevent monopoly where a mark has become common in trade.
